chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), peace be upon him, who said:

There is no cloudy day during which the time of midday (Zawal) is concealed from the people, except that there is a rebuke (Zajrah) from the Imam to the sun until it appears, so that it becomes a proof upon the people of every town, for those who attend to its prayer and for those who neglect it.

key_terms.الزَّجْرَةٌ: A rebuke or command from the Imam to the celestial bodies
key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: The time of midday when the sun reaches its zenith, marking the beginning of Dhuhr prayer

ai.seo_question: How does the Imam ensure the correct time for prayer is known during cloudy days?
ai.summary: In Shia theology, this hadith highlights the Imam’s cosmic authority (Hujjah) over natural phenomena, ensuring the precise timing of Dhuhr prayer remains accessible even under cloud cover. This divine intervention serves as a tangible sign (Ayah) of the Imam’s presence, holding individuals accountable for their observance of prayer based on the clarity of the sun’s appearance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al-Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is none from a cloudy day during which the time of midday is concealed from the people, except that there would be a rebuke by the Imamasws to the sun until it appears, so it would be a proof upon the people of every town, the ones who attend its Salāt and the ones who waste it’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al- Rahman from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that even on cloudy days when the time for noon Salah (prayer) may remain obscure to people, the Imam knows about the sun. (He (the Imam) knows) what is unseen to people, so he always has the proof which town’s people pay attention to the timing of Salah (prayer) and which town’s people ignore it.”
